title: Topics by Hand: Publish, Subscribe and the Order Things Happen In

questions.question: What problem does a topic solve?
options: Two threads writing one variable at once, which a topic serialises through a lock
The publisher and subscriber need to know a name and not each other, so a part can be replaced or a second consumer added without changing the first
Messages arriving out of order, which a topic sorts by the time they were sent
A slow consumer holding up a fast producer, which a topic prevents by copying the payload
questions.explanation: With direct calls every new consumer means editing the producer. With a name between them, the producer never learns who is listening, so parts can be swapped or added without touching it.

questions.question: A message is published to a topic with no subscribers. What should happen?
options: It is dropped and counted: two such messages gave a dropped count of 2, and a subscriber who came later heard only 1 of 3
It is kept until the first subscriber arrives, so that the subscriber who came later heard all 3 of 3
The publish fails with an error, because a message with nobody to receive it is a bug in the program
It is delivered to the subscribers of every other topic, so that it is not lost without a trace
questions.explanation: A publisher cannot know who is listening and should not have to. The bus counts what it drops, and what was published before a subscriber arrived is gone.

questions.question: A handler unsubscribes a later subscriber during delivery. What does the bus do?
options: Calls it anyway, since the list was fixed when the message went out, so the first message reached all 3 subscribers
Skips it: the tokens are copied when the message goes out and each is checked before its call, so b was not called and the first message reached 2 subscribers
Stops the delivery at once, so the first message reached only the 1 subscriber that had already been called
Defers the removal until the delivery has finished, so b was called once more and was gone for the second message
questions.explanation: The list changes under the loop that walks it. Copying the tokens and checking each before its call means a removed subscriber is skipped and nothing is read past the end.

questions.question: A handler publishes a message while handling one. When is it delivered?
options: At once, inside the handler, so the log showed out heard 7 before second heard 7 and the publish returned 1
Only when the next message is published from outside, so it waited and the publish returned 0
Before the rest of the first message's subscribers, since a newer message is more urgent than an older one
After every subscriber of the first message has been called: the publish returned 0 and the log showed second heard 7 before out heard 7
questions.explanation: A message published from a handler waits in a queue. Every subscriber of the first message is called before the second starts, and the stack does not deepen with each hop.

questions.question: Why does the queue stop a ping and a pong that answer each other from overflowing the stack?
options: It limits how many times a topic may publish to another: 5000 each and then it stops them
It runs each handler on its own thread, so neither waits for the other to return
It turns the recursion into a loop: 5000 each ran with no nesting
It drops a message whose topic is already being delivered, so the loop never forms
questions.explanation: Each publish from a handler returns at once and the message is delivered later from the queue, so nothing nests. The bus cannot tell that the two will never stop.

questions.question: What does this bus not do yet?
options: It is one thread with a string payload and no loss or delay: threads, typed payloads and a network are the later lessons
It cannot deliver in order: messages on one topic may overtake each other until a later lesson adds a sequence number
It cannot unsubscribe: a handler stays registered for the life of the bus
It cannot have two subscribers on one topic: fan out is a later lesson
questions.explanation: This first bus is the smallest that shows the idea. What a real one adds, threads, typed payloads, loss and delay, each gets a lesson.
